records.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
records.reason: YaRN extends context windows for RoPE-based LLMs. The paper states that Dynamic Scaling updates the positional-embedding scale on each inference pass, and that the rotary embeddings have zero added overhead; it demonstrates extended LLaMA context lengths up to 64K and 128K. This is an inference-time long-context method, even though some YaRN variants also use limited fine-tuning.

records.title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models
records.reason: LongLoRA's efficiency contribution is reducing compute and GPU memory for fine-tuning long-context models using shifted sparse attention and LoRA. The paper explicitly retains full dense attention for inference and says the sparse attention is optional at inference; it presents no inference-time serving or decoding optimization. The workflow excludes training-only efficiency work, so this is unrelated to the current scope.

records.title: LongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression
records.reason: LongLLMLingua proposes inference-time prompt compression for long-context LLMs. Its budget controller allocates different compression ratios across prompt parts, then iterative token-level compression and document reordering preserve question-relevant content. The paper evaluates both quality and efficiency on GPT-3.5 Turbo and LongChat; the method directly lowers the prompt workload and targets long-context inference cost and position bias.

records.title: Hydra: Sequentially-Dependent Draft Heads for Medusa Decoding
records.reason: Hydra makes speculative draft heads sequentially dependent to improve candidate quality for Medusa-style decoding. Hydra++ reports up to 1.31x decoding throughput over Medusa and 2.70x over autoregressive decoding; batched inference and typical-acceptance sampling are also evaluated. The work directly accelerates LLM decoding.

records.title: Ouroboros: Generating Longer Drafts Phrase by Phrase for Faster Speculative Decoding
records.reason: Ouroboros improves draft generation and speculative decoding without model fine-tuning by generating/reusing phrases and verifying longer candidates in parallel. The primary source reports up to 2.8x speedup over speculative decoding and 3.9x over autoregressive decoding without generation-quality loss; conclusion reports 2.8x and 1.9x against speculative and lookahead decoding, respectively. This directly accelerates LLM inference.

records.title: LLM-PQ: Serving LLM on Heterogeneous Clusters with Phase-Aware Partition and Adaptive Quantization
records.reason: LLM-PQ jointly chooses phase-aware model partitioning, mixed-precision quantization and microbatch size for LLM serving on heterogeneous GPU clusters, optimizing inference throughput under user-specified quality targets. records.title: QuaRot: Outlier-Free 4-Bit Inference in Rotated LLMs
records.reason: QuaRot applies rotations to remove outliers and enable end-to-end 4-bit LLM quantization across weights, activations and KV cache. For Llama 2 70B it reports retaining 99% of FP16 downstream performance, a 2.16x prefill speedup on RTX 3090 and up to 3.39x decode-stage memory savings. This directly improves LLM inference efficiency through quantization.

records.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
records.reason: Mixture-of-Depths learns a router that skips transformer blocks for selected tokens, reducing per-forward-pass FLOPs. Its autoregressive evaluation shows a causal predictor can reproduce trained top-k routing with minimal degradation, and its discussion explicitly states that this tunes per-pass compute and inference time. While substantial experiments measure training/isoFLOP behavior, the primary paper verifies autoregressive sampling and supports inference-time execution, so it is relevant to adaptive inference computation.

records.title: RAGCache: Efficient Knowledge Caching for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.reason: RAGCache reuses intermediate states of retrieved documents across requests in a GPU/host multilevel cache and overlaps vector retrieval with LLM inference. Against vLLM+Faiss it reports up to 4x lower TTFT and 2.1x throughput; against SGLang it reports up to 3.5x lower TTFT and 1.8x throughput. This directly optimizes RAG inference.

records.title: SpinQuant: LLM Quantization with Learned Rotations
records.reason: SpinQuant learns rotations that improve post-training quantization of LLM weights, activations and KV cache. The paper evaluates 4-bit quantization across LLMs and states that one variant merges learned rotations into weights before inference; the online Hadamard variant adds approximately 8% network latency. It directly studies inference-time memory/latency versus quantization accuracy.

records.title: Towards Efficient Mixture of Experts: A Holistic Study of Compression Techniques
records.reason: The paper evaluates Layer Drop, Block Drop, expert quantization, and pruning for MoE inference efficiency. On Mixtral-8x7B, combined trimming and quantization are reported to provide up to 6.05x speedup at 20.0 GB memory, a 77.1% reduction, while retaining over 92% of original performance. Its objective and measured results directly concern MoE inference computation and memory.

records.title: Post-Training Sparse Attention with Double Sparsity
records.reason: Double Sparsity reduces LLM inference KV-cache access using token and channel sparsity, with optional offloading. The primary paper evaluates Llama-2-7B and other LLMs, reporting a minimum 1.3x throughput gain and near-2x in some tested conditions; the offload variant reports 4–8x over FlexGen on regular workloads and up to 16x on 64K–256K long sequences. This is directly inference-time attention and memory optimization.

records.title: No Request Left Behind: Tackling Heterogeneity in Long-Context LLM Inference with Medha
records.reason: Medha combines preemptive chunked prefills, Stream Pipeline Parallelism, KV-Cache Parallelism, dynamic batch packing and a length-aware scheduler for heterogeneous long-context inference. On stated workloads it reports 5.7× throughput over state-of-the-art non-preemptive systems and up to 30× lower median latency and 174× lower P99 latency. Direct serving optimization.

records.title: AMUSD: Asynchronous Multi-Device Speculative Decoding for LLM Acceleration
records.reason: AMUSD lets draft and verify models run continuously and asynchronously on separate devices, with rollback handling to preserve consistency. Its evaluation uses Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-1B across several benchmarks; it reports up to 1.96× speedup over autoregressive decoding and identical output quality, including improved utilization through concurrent GPU execution. This directly targets LLM decoding latency and throughput.

records.title: Context Parallelism for Scalable Million-Token Inference
records.reason: The paper presents context parallelism for long-context LLM inference, including lossless pass-KV and pass-Q ring-attention variants for full prefill, partial prefill and decoding. It reports near-linear scaling to 128 H100 GPUs; a 1M-token prefill for Llama 3 405B in 77 seconds with 93% parallelization efficiency and 63% FLOPS utilization, and 128K prefill in 3.8 seconds. This directly addresses inference scalability and latency.

records.title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
records.reason: The primary title differs from the worklist title, but the identity and paper match. SuffixDecoding uses suffix trees over prompts and prior outputs to reuse repeated token sequences in speculative decoding, especially in agent workflows. The source evaluates OpenHands and AgenticSQL and reports a 5.3x average speedup over vanilla decoding on agentic tasks for the suffix-tree approach; open-ended WildChat/Magicoder results are also reported. This directly accelerates LLM generation/inference.
